title: Naturality of Ext-cohomology for locally free first arguments
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\mathcal F,\mathcal F'$ be finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules, let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $u:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$. Under the canonical isomorphisms $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\cong H^i(X,\mathcal F^\vee\otimes\mathcal G)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F',\mathcal G)\cong H^i(X,(\mathcal F')^\vee\otimes\mathcal G)$ of [lem-sc-ext-locally-free], pullback of extensions along $u$ is the cohomology map induced by $u^\vee\otimes 1$. In particular, for $X=\mathbf P^1_k$ with $k$ an algebraically closed field, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O(d)$, $\mathcal F'=\mathcal O$, $\mathcal G=\omega_{\mathbf P^1}\cong\mathcal O(-2)$ and $u=s:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O(d)$ given by a global section, the composite $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal O(d),\omega)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal O,\omega)=H^1(X,\omega)$ is multiplication by $s$ on Cech cochains, using [def-sc-p1-standard] and [lem-sc-p1-monomial](iii).

proof.text: The evaluation isomorphism for a finite locally free first argument is compatible with precomposition: the square identifying $u^\vee\otimes1$ with $(-)\circ u$ commutes by the first-variable naturality statement [lem-sc-ext-evaluation-first-naturality].

source.place: proof, Step 1: naturality of the locally free evaluation map

proof.text: Read $\operatorname{Ext}$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] (the corrected form of [def-sc-ext-sheaf]: $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=R^i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-)(\mathcal G)$, computed by an injective resolution $\varepsilon:\mathcal G\to I^\bullet$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$). By that node the class of a cocycle $f:\mathcal F\to I^i$ is $\varepsilon[i]^{-1}\circ f$, so pullback along $u$ (precomposition with $u$) is induced by the cochain map $f\mapsto f\circ u$, i.e. by the natural transformation $\operatorname{Hom}(u,-):\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F',-)$. Put $T=\mathcal F^\vee\otimes-$, $T'=(\mathcal F')^\vee\otimes-$ and $\alpha=u^\vee\otimes1:T\to T'$. The canonical isomorphism of [lem-sc-ext-locally-free] is (as constructed there) the composite of this identification, the isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,-)\cong\Gamma(X,T(-))$ given by [lem-sc-ext-evaluation] and the global-sections clause of [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and the isomorphism $R^i(\Gamma(X,-)\circ T)(\mathcal G)\cong\mathrm H^i(X,T\mathcal G)$ of [lem-sc-ext-derived-composite]; the hypotheses of the latter (enough injectives, $T$ exact, $T(I)$ $\Gamma$-acyclic for injective $I$) are verified in [lem-sc-ext-locally-free] for any finite locally free first argument, so for $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F'$ alike. Global sections of the commuting square of [lem-sc-ext-evaluation-first-naturality] (taken with $\mathcal G$ replaced by each $I^n$) show that under the second isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(u,-)$ corresponds to $\Gamma(X,\alpha)$. Finally [lem-sc-ext-derived-composite-natural], applied to $\alpha$ and $U=\Gamma(X,-)$, carries the map induced by $\Gamma(X,\alpha)$ to $\mathrm H^i(X,\alpha_{\mathcal G})=\mathrm H^i(X,u^\vee\otimes1_{\mathcal G})$. Composing the three squares, pullback along $u$ is the cohomology map induced by $u^\vee\otimes1$.

source.place: proof, Step 1: Ext of a finite locally free sheaf and naturality of the canonical identification

proof.text: For $X=\mathbf P^1_k$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O(d)$, $\mathcal F'=\mathcal O$, and $u=s$ given by a global section, write $s|_{U_i}=\sigma_i g_i$ with the generators $g_0,g_1$ of [def-sc-p1-standard]. The dual $\mathcal O(d)^\vee$ is trivialized over $U_i$ by the dual generators $g_i^\vee$ ($g_i^\vee(g_i)=1$), and $u^\vee(g_i^\vee)=\sigma_i$, so $u^\vee\otimes1:\mathcal O(d)^\vee\otimes\omega\to\mathcal O^\vee\otimes\omega=\omega$ is, in these trivializations, multiplication by $\sigma_i$ on $U_i$ (and by $\sigma_0$ on $U_{01}$), i.e. multiplication by $s$ after $\mathcal O(d)^\vee\cong\mathcal O(-d)$. Both sheaves are quasi-coherent (locally free of rank one on $U_0,U_1$), and $U_0,U_1,U_{01}$ are affine [def-sc-p1-standard], so by [lem-pc-cech-computes] their cohomology is the Cech cohomology of the standard cover, and by [lem-sc-cech-comparison-natural] the map $\mathrm H^1(X,u^\vee\otimes1)$ is induced by the cochain map applying $u^\vee\otimes1$ componentwise; on Laurent cochains on $U_{01}$ this is the product with $s$.

source.place: proof, Step 1: the multiplication pairing on the standard Cech cover

proof.text: The resulting composite $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal O(d),\omega)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal O,\omega)=H^1(X,\omega)$ is therefore multiplication by $s$ on Cech cochains. The basis and the identification $\omega\cong\mathcal O(-2)$ are exactly the assertions of [lem-sc-p1-monomial](iii), and the stated basis calculation is [lem-sc-p1-monomial](ii).
